title: Scale hysteresis & metric jitter caused intermittent cold-starts and latency drift — postmortem and action plan
creator: Aisha Raman
summary: Between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-09 we observed repeated latency degradation and sporadic cold-start spikes in the 'inference-router' service despite available capacity. Investigation showed conflicting stabilization windows and percentile-based smoothing across HPA and KEDA metrics which caused delayed scale-ups during short bursts. This ticket captures timeline, root cause, immediate mitigations, and action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-08 01:12 UTC — First user report: increased tail latency for the inference-router route (alerts triggered by SLO monitor).
2026-03-08 01:25 UTC — Automated paging; on-call runbook executed — observed warm-pool not meeting expected size during burst.
2026-03-08 01:40 UTC — Metrics: KEDA scaler 'redis-queue' showed multiple transient trigger spikes; HPA CPU/req-per-second metrics smoothed at 5m percentile.
2026-03-08 02:10 UTC — Engineering triage: hypothesis formed that metric smoothing + probe jitter prevented timely scale-up.
2026-03-08 03:05 UTC — Short-term mitigation deployed: reduced HPA stabilization window from 5m to 60s for inference-router; increased KEDA poll frequency from 30s to 10s.
2026-03-08 04:22 UTC — Latency returned near baseline; SLO alerts cleared.
2026-03-09 12:00 UTC — Review of historical telemetry showed repeated microbursts over 48h that previously were masked by 5m smoothing.
observed_metrics: Instance warm-pool utilization dropped to 40% of target within 30s of burst onset
KEDA Redis scaler observed 2-3x short-lived queue depth spikes (15-45s)
HPA reactive scale events were delayed by stabilization window, causing oscillation once scale finally happened
root_cause: A combination of (1) conservative HPA stabilization windows (5 minutes) designed to prevent flapping, (2) percentile-based smoothing on custom request-rate metrics that suppressed short bursts, and (3) noisy Redis queue depth signals due to a new multiplexing change in the queue consumer introduced in runtime-1.20. Together these prevented timely scale-up for 15-45s microbursts and forced cold-starts that caused the observed latency drift.
immediate_mitigation: Lowered HPA stabilization window for critical inference-router deployment from 5m -> 60s (config patch deployed runtime-1.22).
Increased KEDA scaler polling frequency from 30s -> 10s for Redis scaler for critical services.
Temporarily disabled percentile smoothing on the custom req/s metric used by HPA for inference-router (reverted to raw 15s rate window).
Expanded warm-pool minimum instances for inference-router by +20% for 72 hours to smooth transitions while changes validated.
resolution: After mitigating changes the service returned to expected latency within 90 minutes. We recorded no additional customer-facing incidents tied to this root cause in the next 7 days. Monitoring dashboards were extended to highlight microburst behavior and warm-pool drain during short spikes.
long_term_action_items: Implement multimodal scaler policy that allows short-burst fast-path: KEDA-driven instant triggers + HPA gradual stabilization for sustained load (owner: Marco Delgado, ETA: 2026-04-08).
Introduce a cross-check metric to KEDA scalers that debounces producer-side multiplex bursts (owner: SRE team, ETA: 2026-03-28).
Audit all services using percentile-smoothing metrics for HPA and create guidance doc (owner: Observability, ETA: 2026-04-01).
Add synthetic microburst load tests to CI for inference-router to validate autoscaler behavior under 10-60s spikes (owner: Eng Reliability, ETA: 2026-04-15).
Add warm-pool health reporting to Console with delta-by-route so teams can see warm capacity vs recent burst demand (owner: Console UX, ETA: 2026-05-01).
short_term_followups: Roll back percentile smoothing only after multimodal scaler proof-of-concept is validated.
Run 48h elevated telemetry retention for inference-router metrics to help future investigations.
Schedule walkthrough with platform customers who reported issues to review impact and expected behavior.
rollback_plan: If downstream regressions appear (higher error-rate or flapping), revert HPA stabilization window to prior value and restore percentile smoothing. Rollback will be coordinated with on-call and take ~10 minutes via k8s rollout undo. Contact SRE rotation lead before rollback.
acceptance_criteria: No repeat incidents of 95th latency > 800ms for inference-router during 1-week validation under normal traffic.
Multimodal scaler prototype demonstrates <10s median scale-up for 30s bursts in CI microburst test.
Documentation updated: HPA/KEDA guidance doc published and linked in Console autoscale settings.
notes: This postmortem highlights a broader platform tension: preventing flapping while still reacting to short, customer-visible bursts. The immediate config changes reduce the risk of missed microbursts but also raise flapping risk; the planned multimodal scaler is intended to provide both safety and agility. Follow-ups should prioritize automated tests and clearer telemetry for teams to understand trade-offs.
